item.title: China’s Flatter Bond Curve Shows Deeper Policy Divide With Peers
item.description: A relentless drop in China’s long-end yields is driving an aggressive curve flattening, laying bare a stark macro rift with global markets where long-dated rates have hit multi-year peaks.

item.title: Hong Kong Exchanges’ Non-Equity Push Seen as Key for Stock Boost
item.description: With record trading volumes and new listings providing little boost for shares of Hong Kong Exchanges & Clearing Ltd., analysts are increasingly looking for a jolt from the company’s expansion of non-equity business.

item.title: Unitree Robotics Set to Debut After $904 Million Shanghai IPO
item.description: Unitree Robotics is set to begin trading in Shanghai Wednesday after raising 6.1 billion yuan ($904 million) in an initial public offering that will make it the first publicly traded humanoid robot maker in mainland China.

item.title: AI Boom and Energy Shocks See Growth in Southeast Asia Bifurcate
item.description: Vietnam retained its crown as Southeast Asia’s fastest-growing major economy in the second quarter, with Thailand the laggard, as tech and energy dictated varied fortunes across the region.

item.title: Japan’s Earnings Surprise Analysts to Fuel Bets for Broad Rally
item.description: Japanese companies posted their largest earnings beat in five years despite soaring oil costs, fueling hopes that strong profit growth across sectors can broaden the market rally beyond AI-related trades.

item.title: Chip Rout Clouds Asia Open as Bond Jitters Linger: Markets Wrap
item.description: Stocks in Asia were set to fall Wednesday after a selloff in US technology shares, as elevated bond yields, rising oil prices and renewed Middle East tensions prompted investors to pare risk.

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Aug. 19
item.description: Oil rose for a fourth day, with no sign of progress toward a resolution of the US-Iran war after almost six months of conflict.

item.title: Fletcher Building Waiting on Meaningful Recovery in NZ Demand
item.description: New Zealand’s largest construction materials company Fletcher Building Ltd. doesn’t expect a meaningful recovery in its markets until 2027, adding to signs of muted economic growth over the second half of this year.

item.title: Uruguay Holds Interest Rates Steady With Inflation Below Target
item.description: Uruguay’s central bank held interest rates steady for a fourth consecutive policy meeting with inflation below its target.

item.title: Mizuho Markets Head Expects BOJ to Raise Rates Soon, More Often
item.description: Mizuho Financial Group Inc. expects the Bank of Japan to pick up the pace of interest-rate hikes, with the next one coming as soon as next month, as the weak yen and inflation prompt the central bank to act more quickly.

item.title: Anthropic Plans to Give CEO Extra Voting Power, Information Says
item.description: Anthropic PBC plans to give Chief Executive Officer Dario Amodei and other co-founders shares with extra voting power as the firm prepares to make its Wall Street debut, The Information reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Bond Traders Are Hedging Risk Fed Pivots to Rate Cuts in 2027
item.description: Bond traders are changing gears again. After a raft of data helped all but price out interest rate hikes for the rest of the year, wagers in the options market are looking to hedge the risk that the Federal Reserve pivots to cutting rates in 2027.

item.title: Ripple’s Brokerage Arm Taps Private Placement Bond Market
item.description: The prime-brokerage arm of digital-asset company Ripple has raised $275 million through the private placement bond market.

item.title: KKR Real Estate Lender’s Woes Attract Distressed Investor Mavik
item.description: A hedge fund that specializes in commercial real estate distress is betting that a lender managed by KKR & Co. is likely to sell its loan portfolio at or around book value.

item.title: A Rare Divergence Has Emerged in the Government Bond Market
item.description: 30-year and 2-year bonds on a different direction of travel.

item.title: Mexico Weighs Tougher Trade Rules for China as US Talks Grind On
item.description: Mexico is weighing plans to impose further trade restrictions on selected products from China and other countries while raising existing import taxes on others, according to four people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Late Billionaire’s Heirs Claim Venezuela Seized Oil Assets
item.description: The heirs of late Latin American mogul Oswaldo Cisneros accused the Venezuelan government of unjustly confiscating oil-drilling rights and awarding them to a US company.

item.title: Texas Grid Predicts Record Demand as Heat Rises, Wind Power Sags
item.description: The largest Texas grid is bracing for another bout of searing heat that threatens to topple its all-time power demand record yet again, just as wind generation is predicted to take a dive.

item.title: Crippling Blackouts Put Venezuela’s Industrial Recovery at Risk
item.description: Venezuelan manufacturers lacked grid power for nearly half of their working hours in the second quarter, as the tottering electricity system holds back the economic recovery.

item.title: SEC Unveils Crypto Plan as Agency Moves Ahead on Digital Assets
item.description: The Securities and Exchange Commission unveiled a proposal to exempt certain digital asset offerings from securities registration statements, as the regulator moves ahead with crypto plans after landmark legislation stalled in Congress.

item.title: Pennsylvania Governor Shapiro Puts ‘Guardrails’ on Data Centers
item.description: Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro ordered strict new guardrails on data centers in the state as local opposition grows against developers.

item.title: Ex-Tricolor Executives Face SEC Lawsuit After Firm Collapse
item.description: Tricolor Holdings founder Daniel Chu, who already faces federal charges, and two other former executives were sued by the US Securities and Exchange Commission for allegedly defrauding investors before the used car seller and subprime lender imploded.

item.title: Trump Overhaul Prompts Dulles Board to Seek $14 Billion in Bonds
item.description: The governing board that oversees Washington Dulles International Airport will vote Wednesday on whether to add $15.5 billion to its capital budget to finance the airport’s multi-year overhaul backed by President Donald Trump.

item.title: Boeing-Lockheed Space Venture Inks $1.5 Billion Private Bonds
item.description: Boeing Co. and Lockheed Martin Corp.’s rocket joint venture is wrapping up a $1.5 billion private-bond deal that’s been tripled in size.

item.title: TikTok Is Exploring Feature to Send Money Over Direct Messages
item.description: TikTok is exploring a feature that would allow users to send money to each other in direct messages, in a move that would extend the social media app’s push into financial services.

item.title: Five Grain Ships Struck Near Russian Black Sea Ports
item.description: At least five grain ships have been attacked near the Russian Black Sea ports of Novorossiysk and Tuapse as Moscow struggles to continue exporting grain amid heightened Ukrainian strikes, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: OpenAI Makes AI Safety Changes in Wake of Hugging Face Breach
item.description: OpenAI said it’s implementing more aggressive systems to monitor and safeguard artificial intelligence models under development after recent cybersecurity incidents ignited concerns about AI tools running amok.

item.title: Walter Probe Weighs on Carvana as Investors Suspect Share Sale
item.description: Shares of online used-car dealer Carvana Co. are extending losses Tuesday, hurt by concerns that one of the company’s largest investors — billionaire Mark Walter — may sell down his stake as he contends with a federal probe of his investment empire.

item.title: University of California System Offloads $1 Billion of Private Equity Stakes
item.description: The University of California system sold $1 billion of private equity stakes to HarbourVest Partners, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Meta Exploits Youths on Social Media, States Allege at Trial
item.description: Meta Platforms Inc. has deceived the public for years by targeting children on Facebook and Instagram with technology designed to turn them into compulsive users and drive up advertising revenue, a lawyer at the California attorney general’s office told a jury.
